name: What is the boundary problem of consciousness?
statement: What determines the boundary of a single conscious experience, and why does one unified field of experience stop where it does instead of merging with others?
status_source: Wikipedia, Binding problem: "The boundary problem is another unsolved problem in neuroscience and phenomenology"

name: How does the brainstem modulate dream content?
statement: How does brainstem activation during sleep shape the content of dreams, and can the modulation described by the activation-synthesis hypothesis be measured quantitatively?
status_source: Wikipedia, Activation-synthesis hypothesis: "The mechanics of modulation are not known at this time"

name: How can non-physical qualia affect the brain?
statement: If subjective experiences are not physical, how could they have any effect on brain activity or behaviour, given that physical events seem to have complete physical causes?
status_source: Wikipedia, Qualia: "it becomes unclear how they can have any effect on the brain"

name: What is the neural source of the internal clock for time perception?
statement: What produces the pulses that the brain counts to estimate duration, and which brain structures or circuits implement the internal clock proposed by pacemaker-accumulator models?
status_source: Wikipedia, Time perception: "The source and nature of the pulses is unclear"

name: How does the adult brain perceive form from stationary viewing?
statement: How does the adult visual system recover the shape and form of an object from a stationary view, and which computations in visual cortex carry out this recognition?
status_source: Wikipedia, Form perception: "adult abilities to perceive form from stationary viewing are not fully understood"

name: Why do some animals sleep with one brain hemisphere at a time?
statement: What is the function of unihemispheric slow-wave sleep in birds and aquatic mammals, and does the asymmetry seen in flying birds match that seen in resting ones?
status_source: Wikipedia, Unihemispheric slow-wave sleep: "Much is still unknown about the usage of unihemispheric slow-wave sleep"

name: What mechanism causes cerebral polyopia?
statement: By what mechanism does damage to the occipital or temporal lobes make a patient see two or more repeated images of a single object after fixation?
status_source: Wikipedia, Cerebral polyopia: "though the exact mechanism remains unclear"

name: What is the function of the cortisol awakening response?
statement: What is the biological function of the sharp rise in cortisol shortly after waking, and does it prepare the body for the stress of the coming day?
status_source: Wikipedia, Cortisol awakening response: "The function of cortisol awakening response is unknown"

name: Which metaphysical conclusion does the explanatory gap support?
statement: What does the difficulty of explaining how physical properties give rise to felt experience show about the nature of mind, and which metaphysical view should follow?
status_source: Wikipedia, Explanatory gap: "no consensus about what metaphysical conclusions the existence of the gap"

name: What makes the human brain uniquely adapted to language?
statement: What feature of the human brain makes it uniquely suited to language, given that apes and monkeys have analogues of the same language regions?
status_source: Wikipedia, Neurobiological origins of language: "what makes the human brain uniquely adapted to language is unclear"

name: Which animals are capable of feeling pain?
statement: Which organisms are capable of experiencing pain, and what evidence from behaviour or neural structure could settle that question across the animal kingdom?
status_source: Wikipedia, Animal consciousness: "there is no consensus about which organisms are capable of experiencing pain"

name: What adaptive advantage does consciousness provide?
statement: What adaptive advantage could consciousness provide, if evolution cannot tell a conscious organism from a non-conscious one that performs the same function?
status_source: Wikipedia, Neural correlates of consciousness: "it is unclear what adaptive advantage consciousness could provide"

name: Do animals dream under general anesthesia?
statement: Do animals dream while under general anesthesia, and can any measurable signal separate dreaming from unconsciousness in an anesthetized brain?
status_source: Wikipedia, Anesthesia: "It is not known whether animals dream while under general anesthesia"

name: What causes phantom limb pain?
statement: What causes the pain that most amputees feel in a limb that is gone, and does somatosensory cortex reorganisation or activation explain it?
status_source: Wikipedia, Phantom limb: "This phenomenon is still not fully understood"

name: What causes phantom vibrations of a mobile phone?
statement: Why do people perceive their phone vibrating or ringing when it is not, and what cognitive or neural process produces the false sensation?
status_source: Wikipedia, Phantom vibration syndrome: "The cause of phantom vibrations is not known"

name: What causes posterior cortical atrophy?
statement: What causes posterior cortical atrophy, the visual variant of dementia, and what diagnostic criteria can the clinical community fully accept?
status_source: Wikipedia, Posterior cortical atrophy: "The cause of PCA is unknown"

name: Does recall create a new memory or retrieve a reconsolidated one?
statement: When an old situation is recalled, does the brain form a new memory or reconsolidate the original, and how could the two be told apart experimentally?
status_source: Wikipedia, Memory: "It is still not known whether or not these are new memories"

name: What is the total capacity of long-term memory?
statement: How much information can long-term memory hold, and what measure of capacity applies to a biological memory system?
status_source: Wikipedia, Memory: "the total capacity of long-term memory has yet to be established"

name: What is the function of mirror neurons in macaques?
statement: What function do mirror neurons serve in macaques, which fire both when the animal acts and when it watches the same action?
status_source: Wikipedia, Mirror neuron: "The function of mirror neurons in macaques remains unknown"

name: Do young children understand the syntactic rules of their language?
statement: At the stage of early two-word sentences, do children understand the underlying rules of their language, such as syntactic categories?
status_source: Wikipedia, Language development: "unclear whether children have an understanding of underlying rules of the language"

name: Is there a consensus definition of autistic burnout?
statement: Can researchers agree on one definition and set of diagnostic features for autistic burnout, given the several competing characterisations proposed so far?
status_source: Wikipedia, Autism: "no consensus definition exists"

name: Should large language models be viewed as models of the human mind?
statement: If and how should large language models be treated as models of the human brain or human mind, and what evidence would support such a claim?
status_source: Wikipedia, Large language model: "it is unclear if or how LLMs should be viewed as models"

name: How can mental disorders be defined in a culturally neutral way?
statement: Can a definition of mental disorders be written that does not depend on the cultural norms of the Western authors of diagnostic manuals?
status_source: Wikipedia, Unsolved problems in medicine: "a culturally neutral definition of mental diseases is an unsolved problem"

name: Can mental disorders be classified by their cause?
statement: Can psychiatry group mental disorders by cause instead of by symptoms, as medicine does for paralysis or kidney failure, and would that improve treatment?
status_source: Wikipedia, Unsolved problems in medicine: "grouping mental disorders by their cause is still an unsolved problem"

name: Why is the diagnosis of major depression unreliable?
statement: Why do independent experts diagnose major depressive disorder inconsistently, with an agreement score near 0.28, and how can psychiatric diagnosis be made reliable?
status_source: Wikipedia, Unsolved problems in medicine: "major depressive disorder is often diagnosed differently by independent experts"

name: How do psychiatric medications help patients?
statement: Does a psychiatric drug correct a specific chemical imbalance, change the balance of brain activity, or only keep the patient manageable?
status_source: Wikipedia, Unsolved problems in medicine: "it is debated how a given medication may help a patient"
